NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A family displaced by a storm asks to stay near the village: welcome them in, or give them supplies for their own camp.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A family whose island was battered by a great storm has arrived in a damaged canoe, with nothing but each other. They ask to camp near the village until they can go home. (subject) wants to bring them right into the village. (friend) thinks they might prefer a camp of their own, and some peace. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The family is given space in the village and food from every hut. They are grateful and overwhelmed. Over a season, working side by side in the gardens, they become neighbors. When their island is rebuilt, half of them go home. Half stay.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village helps them build a camp by the far beach, with supplies and visits whenever they want them. The family keeps its own ways and its own fire. They come to the village feasts and go back to their camp. When they leave, they leave a carved post in thanks.
